findings.title: SPEC-03 dependency on SPEC-04 is contradicted by the module map
findings.location: Section 1 "Module Map"; Section 2 "Seam C: SPEC-03 → SPEC-04"; Section 5 "Review Order"
findings.evidence: "SPEC-03 | Tool-Call Lifecycle | ... | Depends On | SPEC-01" vs "The lifecycle layer emits a `DhfTurnContext` (defined in SPEC-04)" and later "SPEC-03 ... depends on SPEC-01, 02, 04".
findings.problem: The top-level dependency graph is internally inconsistent about whether SPEC-03 consumes SPEC-04.
findings.why_it_matters: This breaks build ordering, ownership boundaries, and architecture-test rules before implementation starts.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the dependency graph consistent in all sections and list the exact SPEC-04 interfaces/types consumed by SPEC-03.

findings.title: DHF append trigger contradicts the stated per-turn ledger granularity
findings.location: Section 2 "Seam C: SPEC-03 → SPEC-04"; Section 3 "Mandatory vs Stretch"; Section 6 "Glossary"
findings.evidence: "Every terminal lifecycle transition produces a DHF write"; "per-turn DHF"; "Turns are the DHF-entry granularity"; "Turn: ... possibly containing 0+ tool calls."
findings.problem: If a turn can contain multiple tool calls, writing on every terminal lifecycle transition conflicts with one DHF entry per turn.
findings.why_it_matters: This blocks schema design, hash-chain semantics, viewer timeline behavior, and acceptance-test expectations.
findings.proposed_fix: Specify whether the ledger appends once per turn or once per tool call; if both are required, define separate record types and their hash-chain relationship.

findings.title: Timeout/cancel semantics are not implementable as written for synchronous STA COM calls
findings.location: Section 2 "Seam B: SPEC-03 → SPEC-02"; Section 6 "Tool-Call Lifecycle State" and "Quarantine"
findings.evidence: "SPEC-02 provides a synchronous method surface; SPEC-03 wraps each call in its own timeout and cancel semantics." and terminal states include "TimedOut" and "Cancelled".
findings.problem: Once a synchronous COM call is dispatched on the STA thread, SPEC-03 cannot reliably cancel it; a timed-out call can continue mutating SolidWorks while the orchestration layer treats it as terminal and quarantines late outcomes.
findings.why_it_matters: This creates ledger/CAD-state divergence, breaks undo-group guarantees, and makes failure handling non-deterministic.
findings.proposed_fix: Define the exact cancellation boundary: pre-dispatch only, cooperative cancellation points inside SPEC-02, or a mandatory post-timeout recovery/lockout flow before subsequent turns.

findings.title: The DTO ownership rule conflicts with `DhfTurnContext` being defined outside the Protocol module
findings.location: Section 2 "Seam A: SPEC-01 → everyone"; Section 2 "Seam C: SPEC-03 → SPEC-04"
findings.evidence: "Architecture rule: no DTO types exist outside `BSVoiceCAD.Protocol.*` namespaces." and "The lifecycle layer emits a `DhfTurnContext` (defined in SPEC-04)".
findings.problem: The document bans DTOs outside Protocol while simultaneously introducing a cross-module data carrier in SPEC-04.
findings.why_it_matters: Architecture tests and module ownership become ambiguous, causing churn over where boundary types belong.
findings.proposed_fix: Either move all cross-module contract types into SPEC-01 or narrow the rule to cross-process wire DTOs and explicitly allow internal module-boundary models.

findings.title: Placing cross-module NetArchTest rules in lower-numbered spec tests inverts the claimed build graph
findings.evidence: "Violations are detected by `NetArchTest` rules living in the test project of the lower-numbered spec."
findings.problem: To verify seams against higher-numbered assemblies, lower-numbered test projects must reference modules that are supposed to depend on them, which undermines the stated leaf-module and review-order model.
findings.why_it_matters: CI/build isolation becomes circular and lower-numbered specs can no longer be built or reviewed independently.
findings.proposed_fix: Move seam-validation rules to a dedicated architecture/integration test project that is allowed to reference all modules.

findings.title: DHF session termination has no crash/disconnect/restart contract
findings.evidence: "Closes when a different AddinSessionId arrives or on orchestrator shutdown."
findings.problem: The contract omits what happens when the add-in crashes, the WebSocket disconnects, the orchestrator is killed, or either side restarts without a clean shutdown.
findings.why_it_matters: Open sessions can remain dangling indefinitely, and viewer/integrity logic cannot determine whether a session ended cleanly or was abandoned.
findings.proposed_fix: Define disconnect detection, heartbeat/timeout rules, restart recovery, and how end reasons are recorded in the ledger.

findings.title: Day-0 validation includes a stretch dependency that the scope says can be descoped
findings.evidence: "voice ... all stretch" and later "Day-0 validation on ... Whisper.net CUDA".
findings.problem: A component listed as stretch is still treated as part of day-0 validation, which makes a descopable feature a practical blocker.
findings.why_it_matters: This creates avoidable schedule risk and inconsistent CI/release criteria.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove Whisper/CUDA from mandatory day-0 validation or explicitly split mandatory and optional validation tracks.

findings.title: AddinSessionId generation is underspecified for uniqueness and testability
findings.evidence: "UUID generated fresh on each add-in load, deterministically from (machineGuid, swProcessId, loadTimestamp)."
findings.problem: The UUID version/hash algorithm, timestamp precision, UTC handling, and source/fallback for `machineGuid` are not defined.
findings.why_it_matters: Session collisions or environment-specific generation differences would corrupt the DHF session epoch and `StateVersion` reset behavior.
findings.proposed_fix: Specify the UUID derivation algorithm, required timestamp precision/timezone normalization, and fallback behavior when `machineGuid` is unavailable.

top_3_must_fix: Resolve the contradiction between per-turn DHF entries and "every terminal lifecycle transition produces a DHF write."
Define realistic timeout/cancel behavior for synchronous STA COM calls so timed-out operations cannot silently mutate CAD state outside the ledger.
Make the dependency graph consistent, especially the SPEC-03 ↔ SPEC-04 relationship, before locking review/build order.
